group_assessment.weighting: Craniofacial developmental-biology group (PRMT1 in neural crest); eLife reviewed preprint, version of record. No WWOX publication; WWOX is one of many long genes in a genome-wide intron-retention screen.

field_density.note: No PubMed record pairs WWOX with intron retention; one pairs it with SFPQ or PRMT1. A trans-acting splicing regulator of Wwox has no prior literature on PubMed by these queries.

multihop.note: 96 references declared (95 ref elements parsed); none concerns WWOX. The Discussion's statement on human WWOX epileptic encephalopathy cites Dvinge and Bradley 2015 (Genome Medicine, PMC4480902), a pan-cancer intron-retention paper whose Europe PMC full text (133 557 B) contains zero occurrences of WWOX, epileptic or encephalopathy: the citation does not support the sentence. No WWOX hop is owed.

entries.proposition: Wwox is named as a 913 kb mouse gene whose retained intron is 639 kb, as an example of long SFPQ-regulated genes.
entries.snippet: Of note, Wnt pathway gene Wwox and matrix genes St6galnac3 are 913 and 526 kb in length, and their retained introns are 639 and 215 kb in length, respectively

entries.snippet: the long gene Wwox exhibited increased retention of long introns (introns 3 and 4) and decreased expression upon Prmt1 or Sfpq deficiency

entries.proposition: Figure 8 caption: SFPQ depletion elevated intron retention and decreased mRNA abundance of the Wnt-signaling genes shown, with significance marked at p < 0.01.
entries.snippet: SFPQ depletion in CNCCs elevated intron retention and decreased mRNA abundance of Wnt signaling components

entries.proposition: PANEL READING. In Figure 8A the Wwox row carries significance stars on the intron-retention bars for both siRNAs (about 0.8% of mRNAs in control versus about 1.2 to 1.4% after knockdown) but NO star on either TPM bar; Wwox TPM is near the axis (a few TPM on a 0-400 scale). The caption's 'decreased mRNA abundance' is not marked significant for Wwox, and the intron-retaining fraction is a small minority of Wwox mRNA.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 8A, Wwox row: right-hand intron-retention bars for siSFPQ#1 and siSFPQ#2 each carry an asterisk and reach roughly 1.2-1.4% against roughly 0.8% for siControl on a 0-10% axis; left-hand TPM bars carry no asterisk and lie within a few TPM of zero on a 0-400 TPM axis.

entries.proposition: The knockdown reduced Sfpq to about half, in three sequenced sets per arm.
entries.snippet: SFPQ knockdown caused around 50% reduction in Sfpq expression in CNCCs

entries.proposition: Sequencing design: five sets of control or Prmt1 CKO neural crest cells and three sets of siControl or siSFPQ cells, 40 million reads, 150 bp paired-end.
entries.snippet: three sets of isolated CNCCs transfected with siControl or siSFPQs were sequenced at 40 million reads sequencing depth and 150 bp paired-end sequencing

entries.proposition: The authors link the Wwox observation to human WWOX epileptic encephalopathy with large intronic deletions, citing a pan-cancer intron-retention paper that does not mention WWOX.
entries.snippet: In human patients, pathogenic variants of WWOX with large deletions within the long introns have been associated with epileptic encephalopathy syndrome manifesting shared facial phenotype

entries.proposition: Shared feature of SFPQ-regulated genes: long genes with long introns; the IR-elevated genes have a median length of about 100 kb versus about 10 kb in controls.
entries.snippet: the genes with increased IR in Sfpq -depleted CNCCs have a median length of ~100 kb
